feedback.label: X-factor (shoulder-hip separation)
feedback.message: Low shoulder-hip separation at the top — less stored coil than typical tour swings.

feedback.label: Posture (spine angle)
feedback.message: Noticeable posture change from address to impact — spine angle shifts more than most tour swings (early extension / standing up).

feedback.label: Head sway
feedback.message: More lateral head movement than typical tour swings — head drifts off the ball during the swing.

feedback.label: Head height
feedback.message: More vertical head movement than typical — head rises/drops more than most tour swings.

summary: 4 indicator(s) fall outside the typical tour range — see notes below.
llm_summary_v2:
Your hip rotation at impact (how open the hips are at impact) was in the tour range. Your spine angle at address (how much the upper body leans forward from standing upright) was also in the tour range. Your weight shift (moving body weight toward the target through the downswing) was in the tour range, and your tempo (the timing and rhythm of the swing) was close to the tour-typical pace.

At the top (the top of the backswing, where the club changes direction), your X-factor (the gap between how far the shoulders turn and how far the hips turn) was lower than most tour swings, so there was less separation between the shoulders and hips than in most tour swings. By impact (the instant the club meets the ball), your spine angle was lower than most tour swings, and your posture (the spine and body angle held during the swing) changed more from address to impact than in most tour swings.

During the backswing (the takeaway and turn back, away from the target), your head sway (sideways movement of the head or body away from the ball) was higher than most tour swings, so the head drifted further side-to-side than most tour swings. During the downswing (the move from the top of the backswing down to the ball), your head height change was also higher than most tour swings, so the head moved more up-and-down than most tour swings. There is still a solid base here to build on.
